For The Photographer

Photographer Guide

The best frames on this trip are edge-of-day seascapes on Oahu, the Milky Way over Mauna Kea on the new-moon night, and Kīlauea's crater glow after dark. Treat midday as family and beach time; shoot dawn, dusk, and one dark night.

📸

Landscape photo spots — Oahu + Big Island

Exact map targets, light timing, iconic + hidden angles, and click-to-open photo galleries. Tap to expand.

 ▾

How to shoot the trip

Chase the edges of the day — and one dark night

The headline Hawaii frames are sunrise seascapes on Oahu's windward coast, the Milky Way over Mauna Kea on the new-moon night (~June 9, 2027), and Kīlauea's after-dark glow. Midday is harsh and crowded — bank it as beach and family time and shoot the golden edges.

Verify Kīlauea's eruption status, air quality (vog), and viewing access before building a night around it; the Mauna Kea summit needs a 4WD and altitude caution (shoot from the 9,200 ft visitor center if unsure); Hanauma Bay needs a timed reservation. Plug each target into PhotoPills once 2027 dates lock.

Useful kit

  • 16-35mm for seascapes, cliffs, the caldera, and tight overlooks.
  • 24-105mm travel zoom for family + landscape flexibility.
  • 70-200mm for surf compression, island layers, and Mauna Kea foregrounds.
  • Fast wide (14-24mm f/2.8) + sturdy tripod for the Milky Way and lava glow.
  • CPL for turquoise water and reefs; 3-6 stop ND for waterfalls and surf.
  • Warm layers + gloves for the freezing Mauna Kea summit; red headlamp for night work.

Base: Oahu

Oahu

June light: sunrise around 5:50, sunset around 19:15. The windward coast (Lanikai, Pali, Hanauma) is the sunrise money; the North Shore is calm in summer and best at golden hour.

Iconic sunrise seascape

Waikiki Beach + Diamond Head

Open map ↗

Exact Location

Diamond Head crater overlooks the 1.5-mile Waikiki shoreline in central Honolulu.

How To Get There

Walk or taxi to Waikiki Beach; the Diamond Head trail is a 1.6-mile hike ($5 entry, opens 6:00 AM). No permit for beach photography.

Best Time

Sunrise 5:50–6:15 for golden light on Diamond Head; blue hour 30 min before for pastels; sunset for a warm glow.

Field Tips

Start 45 min before sunrise for pre-dawn pastels; a CPL cuts glare and saturates the reef water; arrive by 6:30 to beat crowds.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Diamond Head rising from turquoise water at sunrise with the Waikiki skyline (16–35mm).
  • Curved beach, hotels, and crater from the Diamond Head summit.
  • A surfer paddling out at golden hour with the crater framed behind.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from Fort DeRussy Park at the west end looking back at Diamond Head at sunset — fewer crowds.
  • Frame palms and beach umbrellas against the volcano for foreground layers.

Turquoise crater cove

Hanauma Bay Overlook

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A protected marine sanctuary in a natural amphitheater of turquoise water on Kalanianaʻole Hwy.

How To Get There

Free overlook above the lot; beach entry is $7 (reservation required, closed Mon–Tue), open from 6:45 AM. Steep stairs to the sand.

Best Time

Sunrise for soft light on the cliffs; mid-morning 9:00–10:00 for the most saturated turquoise and visible reef.

Field Tips

A polarizer is essential to reveal the reef beneath the surface; a graduated ND balances a bright sky against the darker crater walls.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Wide panorama of the crater bay — turquoise water, dark volcanic cliffs, reef patterns beneath.
  • Elevated view of the curved beach, swimmers, and reef from the overlook.
  • Long shadows raking across the crater floor at sunrise.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Hike the nearby Makapuʻu Lighthouse Trail for an elevated angle over the bay and offshore islands.
  • Shoot the reef detail from the shallows with a CPL, crater walls behind.

White sand + twin islands

Lanikai Beach + Mokulua Islands

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A 2.5-mile stretch of powdery white sand in Kailua, with the twin Mokulua islands offshore.

How To Get There

Free street parking near Kalapawai Market, then a short walk to public beach access. Uncrowded early.

Best Time

Sunrise 5:50–6:20 for backlit sand and the Mokes in silhouette; blue hour for cool, moody tones.

Field Tips

Windward light is often backlit — embrace it for silhouettes and rim light; water is clearest before swimmers churn the sand.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Wide beach curve with the Mokulua islands on the horizon (24–35mm, low from the sand).
  • Twin islands compressed over turquoise water (70–200mm).
  • Islands reflected in wet sand at low tide.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Hike the short Kalapawai path for an elevated view over the beach and islands.
  • Frame the islands through palm trunks and fronds for depth.

Legendary surf + golden hour

North Shore — Waimea, Sunset & Pipeline

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A 2-mile cluster of world-famous breaks along Haleiwa’s north coast; Waimea is calm in summer, Pipeline epic year-round.

How To Get There

Free parking at Waimea Bay or Sunset Beach Park; limited street parking at Pipeline — arrive early. Public access; respect surfers.

Best Time

Sunrise for backlit, glassy water; golden hour 18:45–19:15 for warm tones on breaking waves. June brings smaller, cleaner summer swells.

Field Tips

Bring a 200–400mm to isolate surfers without crowding the lineup; stay clear during dawn patrol (6:00–8:00 AM).

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Silhouetted surfer riding a wave against a warm sky at sunset.
  • Wave crest breaking over the reef with backlit spray.
  • Summer-calm Waimea Bay in soft turquoise and white sand.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from the elevated Kamehameha Hwy roadside for an unobstructed line on Pipeline.
  • Climb the short cliff behind Sunset Beach for a west-facing lineup view.

Dramatic windward vista

Nuʻuanu Pali Lookout

Open map ↗

Exact Location

An 1,186-ft overlook on the Pali Hwy with views of Kāneʻohe, Kailua, and the Koʻolau cliffs.

How To Get There

Drive north from Honolulu on the Pali Hwy; $7 parking, open 6:00 AM. Short walk to the railings. Notoriously windy.

Best Time

Sunrise for soft light on the Koʻolau cliffs and pastel sky; mid-morning for vivid greens and cloud formations.

Field Tips

Winds can exceed 40 mph — use a strap and a fast shutter (1/500+); a graduated ND balances the bright sky against the cliffs.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • 180° panorama of the Koʻolau cliffs down to Kāneʻohe Bay (16–35mm).
  • Jagged ridgeline with clouds weaving between the peaks.
  • Soft light on the patchwork of Kailua and Kāneʻohe below.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from the parking-area edges toward the Pali Pass for fewer photographers and dramatic skies.
  • Catch morning mist rolling over the cliffs for layered, moody frames.

Base: Big Island

Big Island

Kona (leeward) is dry and warm; Hilo (windward) is wet and green. The headline frames are Mauna Kea’s Milky Way on the new-moon night (~June 9) and Kīlauea’s after-dark glow.

Sea cliffs + historic bay

Kealakekua Bay + Captain Cook Monument

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A crescent bay ~12 miles south of Kailua-Kona, ringed by 1,000-ft sea cliffs with a white obelisk across the water.

How To Get There

The monument is visible from Napoʻopoʻo Beach Park (free); for a close-up, kayak (~$35–50/day) or take a boat tour. The hiking trail is steep, ~90 min round-trip.

Best Time

Sunrise for soft backlit cliffs and a monument silhouette; mid-morning 7:30–9:30 for turquoise water detail.

Field Tips

Kayaking at first light gives the best cliff perspective; water clarity is exceptional (80–100 ft) so a CPL pays off. Wear water shoes on the rocky Napoʻopoʻo side.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Monument rising from turquoise water against the massive sea cliffs.
  • Aerial-feeling crescent of bay, reef, and cliffs from the trail rim.
  • Cliffs and monument in golden-hour relief.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from the cliff rim above the bay looking down on monument and reef.
  • Kayak to the eastern edge for the monument with the Kona coast behind.

Milky Way over the summit

Mauna Kea Summit + Milky Way

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A 13,796-ft volcano summit and one of Earth’s best dark-sky sites; the Onizuka Visitor Center (9,200 ft) is the public access point.

How To Get There

Self-drive to the visitor center (free); summit access needs a 4WD and stops 30 min after sunset. Guided stargazing tours handle transport and altitude.

Best Time

Milky Way core visible Mar–Oct; shoot 23:00–4:00 on a new-moon night (~June 9, 2027). Freezing even in summer.

Field Tips

Wide fast lens (14–24mm f/2.8), sturdy tripod; ISO 1600–3200, 15–20 sec, manual focus to infinity. Dress in extreme-cold layers and use a red headlamp.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Milky Way arch spanning the sky over silhouetted cinder cones.
  • Milky Way core over the observatory domes as foreground silhouettes.
  • Star trails or a Milky Way time-lapse above the summit.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from the 9,200-ft visitor center for easier access, less wind, and still-excellent clarity.
  • Walk to a nearby cinder cone for elevated foreground interest.

Black sand + sea turtles

Punaluʻu Black Sand Beach

Open map ↗

Exact Location

A 2-mile stretch of jet-black lava sand ~32 miles southeast of Kona, home to green sea turtles (honu).

How To Get There

Free parking, roadside access, restrooms and showers. Stay 15 ft from turtles, no touching, and no flash.

Best Time

Golden hour for warm tones on the black sand and lava rock; late afternoon 4:00–5:30 for turtle-basking activity.

Field Tips

Black sand fools meters — expose for the dark foreground, not the sky, and use a graduated ND. A 200–400mm keeps a respectful distance from turtles.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Curved black-sand beach with palm framing, turquoise water, and lava formations.
  • White foam breaking on black sand (high-contrast).
  • Silhouetted palms against a golden sunset and dark sand.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Shoot from the low cliff above for the crescent of black sand and turtles.
  • Capture turtle tracks meandering across the sand at low tide.

Caldera + lava glow

Hawaiʻi Volcanoes NP — Kīlauea

Open map ↗

Exact Location

Kīlauea’s summit caldera ~30 miles from Hilo; Halemaʻumaʻu has shown episodic lava-lake glow visible at night from the rim.

How To Get There

Park entry $30/vehicle (7-day). Free rim viewpoints: Uēkahuna, Kīlauea Overlook, Keanakākoʻi, Volcano House. Night viewing is best for the glow.

Best Time

Sunrise for soft light and steam on the crater walls; night 20:00–midnight for the red/orange glow (darkest skies for best color).

Field Tips

Night glow: tripod, 16–24mm, ISO 800–1600, 10–20 sec. Check the NPS site for eruption status and vog; mornings are clearer than afternoons.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Halemaʻumaʻu crater with steaming vents and lava-lake glow at night.
  • Observatory domes silhouetted against the glowing crater.
  • Crater-rim trail with hikers and a dramatic caldera backdrop.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Walk the Crater Rim Trail at dawn to hit several overlooks in one soft-light window.
  • Frame the crater through the historic Volcano House windows at golden hour.

Waterfall with morning rainbow

Rainbow Falls (Waiānuenue), Hilo

Open map ↗

Exact Location

An 80-ft waterfall dropping into a wide pool ~3 miles from Hilo, wrapped in tropical rainforest.

How To Get There

Short 5-min walk to the overlook; $5/person, $7 parking. The lower-pool trail is steep and muddy — wear grippy shoes.

Best Time

Early morning for soft light and mist; late morning 9:30–11:00 often produces the fullest rainbow arcs.

Field Tips

Rainbows sit opposite the sun — morning east light makes the bow visible from the overlook. Fast shutter to freeze the falls, or 2–4 sec to smooth them.

Iconic / Instagram-Worthy Frames

  • Full rainbow arc spanning the mist below the falls (wide-angle).
  • Foreground ferns and ginger with the falls and rainbow behind.
  • Wide panorama of the lush green gorge and falling water.

Hidden / Less Obvious Angles

  • Take the steep lower-pool trail for a closer, more intimate angle.
  • Shoot from the side for an off-axis view of the rainbow and water column.
